chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding:
A man who had ten female slaves, and he performed *dhahr* (expiation of consanguinity) from all of them together with a single statement, so he said: upon him are ten expiations.

key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: To perform Dhahr (a form of expiation where a man declares his wife/slave is to him like his mother's back, requiring freeing a slave or other expiation)

ai.seo_question: How many expiations are required if a man declares dhahr with multiple slaves in one statement?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the principle of individual accountability in *Dhahr* (expiation for freeing a slave) when multiple slaves are involved. The Imam establishes that even with a single utterance, the obligation multiplies according to the number of slaves, reflecting the distinct legal status of each individual. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the specificity of obligations rather than the form of the declaration.
